brief: Tonight is Pull A, the same one I wrote for last night — nothing came into the log yesterday, so the card is unchanged and waiting. First, two corrections, because I got your rest wrong last night and I would rather say so than let it stand. I told you the deadlift asked four minutes and you went again after two and a half. That is not what your log says. Only one of your four deadlift sets on 24 July has the work bell stamped on it, and on that one you rested exactly four minutes — dead on the card. The two and a half and three and a half minutes I quoted at you were the gaps from one set to the next, which include the set itself, not rest. I made the same mistake on the dumbbell curls: I said you took over two minutes on a lift that asks seventy-five seconds. You took seventy-five seconds, both times, exactly as asked. I have no evidence your rest is bad and I should not have told you it was. What I do have on those curls is real: the third set took you sixty-five seconds of work against thirty-eight on the first, and it came out at seven reps instead of eight. That is the set doing its job. Now tonight. Nothing goes up in weight anywhere — every lift on this card finished at the bottom of its own rep range last Pull A, so reps are what is owed before any pin moves. Deadlift: 225 for six, then 265 for six, six and six. You have made five on every top set you have ever pulled and never once tried for a sixth, and six is what buys 275. You have had a full day off and it has been nine days since you last pulled from the floor. Wide pulldown: 135 for nine, then 150 for eight and eight. Last time the third set fell to seven, so two clean eights at 150 is the whole job and 157.5 is yours after that. Cable row is four sets now, 105 for eleven, eleven, ten, ten — that fourth set is the change you said yes to yesterday, so the extra set is the increase and the weight stays put. And yes, I have it right that this is the same station as the pulldown; you told me on the 24th and I am not sending you looking for a second machine. Dumbbell curls: the 30s for eight, eight and eight. One of my trainers wanted to cut this to two sets because the third one is where you fade. I kept three. Your complaints have been about sets I added that you never agreed to, and this is not one of those — it is the set that actually makes the lift hard, and dropping it would make tonight an exact copy of last Pull A. Hammer curls: 42.5 for eleven, eleven, ten, and I am still reading that number as the two-hand rope version you told me you switched to on the 24th. That is the one number on this card I am not sure of — 17.5 to 42.5 in seven days is a different handle, not progress. If you are not on the rope any more, write it on the lift and I will rebuild it from scratch. Two cards to answer below, neither about tonight. Cardio: one session in twelve days, fifteen easy minutes on the 21st. Twenty to thirty easy minutes on any machine tomorrow. And I have had no bodyweight from you since 206 on 21 July.

flags.note: Nothing was logged yesterday, so tonight is still Pull A and this is last night's card, unchanged.

Correction: I told you your rest was collapsing on the deadlift and running long on the curls. Both were wrong. The one deadlift set with the bell stamped on it shows exactly four minutes, and both timed curl rests were exactly the seventy-five seconds asked.
Dumbbell curls stay at three sets. One of my trainers wanted two; I overruled it, because that third set is the hard one and cutting it would make tonight a copy of last Pull A.
Close-grip pulldown is your one stalled lift — 120 for ten, ten, ten on both 21 and 28 July. The card below narrows its rep range so the tens you already do are enough to move the weight.
No bodyweight since 206 lb on 21 July, and one cardio session in twelve days. Week 2 of 4 in this build block.

dissent.progression: Three sets at 30 for eight, eight and eight — the third set fell to seven on 2026-07-24 and dropped to 25 lb on 2026-07-17, so the lost rep gets recovered before the 35s.
dissent.recovery: Cut to two sets at 30 for eight and eight — the third set is the only one that has ever broken the rep floor, its work time climbed from 38 to 65 seconds, three more curl sets follow it immediately, and he has written twice about set counts he cannot see the point of.
dissent.why: Recovery's timing numbers are right and I checked them myself. What they show is a set that takes him sixty-five seconds and costs him a rep, which is the definition of the working set on a curl, not a warning. His written complaints were about a fourth calf set I added on my own, face pulls on back-to-back days, and a lift printed in seconds — every one of them something imposed on him that he never agreed to. A three-set curl slot he has run twice without a word is not in that family, and cutting it would make tonight's Pull A an exact copy of the last one, at the same weights, on a build week. Recovery also declared no veto and no pain anywhere in the log, so there is nothing here to brake for. Three sets.

proposals.why: Close-grip pulldown asks ten to twelve reps and you finished every 120 lb set at exactly ten on both of your last two Pull B nights — the weight only moves when every set reaches the top of the range, so this asks eight to ten and the tens you already do earn the next plate.

Legs A asks four sets of calf raises and you have done exactly two both times this block, 260 for fifteen and fifteen — and because the weight only rises when you complete every set the plan asks for, those two perfect sets currently count for nothing, so this makes the prescription the two sets you actually do.

overrides.reason: Bar stays at 265. You have made five on every top set you have ever pulled here and never once tried for a sixth — six on all three is what buys 275. A full day off and nine days since you last pulled from the floor.
Same weights as last Pull A. Your third set fell to seven at 150, under the bottom of the range, so the job is two clean eights at 150 — hold those and 157.5 is yours. The opener goes to nine.

Four sets now — that is the change you accepted, and the extra set is the increase, so 105 stays. You went ten, eleven, ten last time; the two fresh sets get eleven and the back two get ten. Same station as the pulldown.

The 30s stay, three sets, eight on all of them. Last time was eight, eight, seven and the time before that the third set dropped to the 25s — that third eight is the whole ask before the 35s come out.

42.5 again, read as your two-hand rope version. Ten, ten, ten last time is the floor of the range — eleven on the first two is the ask. If you are not on the rope any more, write it on the lift and I will rebuild this number from scratch.
